entities.summary: Johannes Ockeghem was a Franco-Flemish composer and singer of early Renaissance music, active in the 15th century. Born in Hainaut, Flanders, around 1390, Ockeghem became a prominent figure in the Franco-Flemish School, influencing generations of composers. His innovative use of polyphony and choral music, as seen in his famous motet 'Messe de Nostre Dame,' showcased his mastery of the genre. Ockeghem's collaboration with fellow composer Antoine Busnois led to the creation of some of the most iconic works of the era. His legacy as a key proponent of the Franco-Flemish School continues to inspire composers and musicologists to this day. The exact date of Ockeghem's death remains unknown, but his influence on Western classical music remains unparalleled. As a leading figure in the development of Renaissance polyphony, Ockeghem's contributions to the evolution of musical composition and the Franco-Flemish School cannot be overstated.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Ockeghem's innovative use of polyphony and choral music had a profound impact on the development of Western classical music, influencing generations of composers and shaping the course of Renaissance music.
